description: Composite two-panel Ashby-style property-comparison scatter figure (no micrographs or spectra), both panels sharing the x-axis "Specific yield strength (MPa·cm3g-1), LNT" spanning 0-220 with ticks every 20. (a) plots "Charpy impact energy (J), LNT" (0-500, ticks every 100): a red arrow labelled "Present work" points down to one red circle lying just above the 200 J gridline at a specific yield strength between the 60 and 80 gridlines; the highest datum is a magenta diamond above the 400 J line near 45-50, and red squares cluster at 100-200 J between 120 and 140. (b) plots "Total elongation (%), LNT" (0-150, ticks every 30) and carries the only legend: Fe35Mn6Al0.1C (red circle), Fe30Mn5Al0.3C (red square), Fe28Mn5Al1C (blue triangle), Fe30Mn10Al1C1Si (blue inverted triangle), Fe30Mn0.11C (magenta diamond), (19, 22)Mn0.45C and (19, 22)Mn2Al(0.45, 0.46)C (magenta left/right triangles), 304 (brown circle), 9Ni (olive star), Al0.1CoCrFeNi (cyan pentagon). The "Present work" red circle again lies between the 60 and 90 % gridlines. Panel (a) has no legend and neither panel prints numeric data labels. Together the panels argue that the designed low-carbon low-density steel combines high liquid-nitrogen impact energy and elongation at modest specific yield strength.
measured_quantities: Charpy impact energy (J) at liquid nitrogen temperature
specific yield strength (MPa·cm3g-1) at liquid nitrogen temperature
total elongation (%) at liquid nitrogen temperature

observations.observation: Panel (a) y-axis is labelled "Charpy impact energy (J), LNT" with gridlines from 0 to 500 in steps of 100; panel (b) y-axis is labelled "Total elongation (%), LNT" from 0 to 150 in steps of 30.
Both panels share the x-axis "Specific yield strength (MPa·cm3g-1), LNT", running 0-220 with tick labels at 40, 60, 80, 100, 120, 140, 160, 180, 200 and 220.

A red arrow annotated "Present work" marks a single red-circle datum in each panel; in (a) it lies just above the 200 J gridline and in (b) between the 60 and 90 % gridlines, both at a specific yield strength between the 60 and 80 gridlines.
No numeric values are printed on any data point in either panel; only axis ticks, the two axis titles and the "Present work" annotation are legible text.

Panel (b) carries the only legend, with ten entries: Fe35Mn6Al0.1C (red circle), Fe30Mn5Al0.3C (red square), Fe28Mn5Al1C (blue triangle), Fe30Mn10Al1C1Si (blue inverted triangle), Fe30Mn0.11C (magenta diamond), (19, 22)Mn0.45C (magenta left triangle), (19, 22)Mn2Al(0.45, 0.46)C (magenta right triangle), 304 (brown circle), 9Ni (olive star) and Al0.1CoCrFeNi (cyan pentagon).

In panel (a) the highest Charpy impact energy marker is a magenta diamond lying above the 400 J gridline at a specific yield strength just under 50, whereas all markers with specific yield strength above 100 lie below the 200 J gridline.

In panel (a) the red squares (Fe30Mn5Al0.3C) form a cluster between the 100 and 200 J gridlines at specific yield strengths between 120 and 140, and the olive stars (9Ni) lie near the 150 J gridline over roughly 130-150.

In panel (b) the olive 9Ni stars plot at the lowest elongations, roughly on the 30 % gridline at specific yield strengths of about 130-150, while the cyan Al0.1CoCrFeNi pentagon reaches about the 100 % level at a low specific yield strength near 55.

The caption states the figure compares the studied lightweight steel with reported low-carbon low-density steel [34], high carbon lightweight steel [47,48], low-carbon high manganese steel [29], TWIP steel [46], 304 stainless steels [49], 9Ni steel [51] and HEAs [50] at liquid nitrogen temperature.
The caption states that panel (a) is Charpy impact energy versus specific yield strength and panel (b) is total elongation versus specific yield strength, both at LNT.
The citing text states that the impact energies of the other steels were converted to full-size 10 x 10 x 55 mm specimens for the comparison in Fig. 10(a).

The citing text states that the designed low-carbon lightweight steel shows higher Charpy impact energy than high carbon lightweight steel [47,48] and TWIP steel [46], and superior specific yield strength compared with low-carbon high manganese steel [29] and 304 stainless steels [49].

The citing text states that the ductility of the studied steel is at the same level as austenitic TWIP steel but nearly three times higher than that of 9Ni steel, and that its strength/toughness are comparable to the Al0.1CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy [50].

The citing text refers to this comparison as "Fig. 12" while the caption labels the same figure "Fig. 10" and refers to "Fig. 10(a)" and "Fig. 10(b)"; the numbering is inconsistent between caption and body text.

subfigures.description: Scatter plot of Charpy impact energy (J, LNT; y-axis 0-500, ticks every 100) versus specific yield strength (MPa·cm3g-1, LNT; x-axis 0-220). A red arrow annotated "Present work" marks a single red circle just above the 200 J line at x between 60 and 80. Other markers: magenta diamond above 400 J near x = 45-50; cyan-teal pentagon near 290 J at x ~ 55; another magenta diamond near 270 J at x ~ 50; brown circle near 195 J at x ~ 53; magenta triangles rising from ~30 J to ~80 J over x = 95-110; red squares at 170-195 J for x = 120-130; olive stars near 145-150 J for x = 130-150; blue triangles low (near 70 J at x ~ 150, near 0 J at x = 180-200). No legend or data labels.

Scatter plot of total elongation (%, LNT; y-axis 0-150, ticks every 30) versus the same specific yield strength axis. A red arrow annotated "Present work" points to a red circle between the 60 and 90 % gridlines at x between 60 and 80 (the Fe35Mn6Al0.1C composition). A 10-entry legend identifies all markers: Fe35Mn6Al0.1C, Fe30Mn5Al0.3C, Fe28Mn5Al1C, Fe30Mn10Al1C1Si, Fe30Mn0.11C, (19, 22)Mn0.45C, (19, 22)Mn2Al(0.45, 0.46)C, 304, 9Ni, Al0.1CoCrFeNi. Olive 9Ni stars show the lowest elongation (near the 30 % line) at high specific yield strength (~120-150).

unreadable_items: No numeric data labels are printed for individual markers in either panel; all point coordinates can only be read approximately against the gridlines, so exact Charpy impact energy, specific yield strength and total elongation values per alloy are not determinable from the pixels
